title: Abstract Classes
summary: Master the abstract class keyword in Java: preventing premature instantiation, defining partial blueprints, and enforcing subclass obligations.
learningObjectives: Apply the abstract keyword to class definitions to establish incomplete conceptual blueprints
Identify compiler restrictions preventing direct instantiation (new AbstractClass() error)
Differentiate abstract classes from concrete classes regarding state, methods, and constructors
Design hierarchical base classes that enforce contract fulfillment across subclasses
expectedOutcomes: You can define abstract classes that combine instance state with abstract and concrete methods
You understand why the compiler blocks direct instantiation while permitting reference variables

activities.title: Practical Context: Partial Specifications and Shared Baselines

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: An architect draws a master blueprint for a modern suburban home. It outlines the load-bearing foundation, roof geometry, and electrical conduit conduits. But you cannot sleep inside the blueprint, open its refrigerator, or shelter from the rain under it. It is an incomplete model. A builder must pour actual concrete and erect actual drywall to create an inhabited home.
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: The architectural blueprint is the `abstract class`. You cannot instantiate it directly (`new Blueprint()`). The physical houses built on suburban plots are the concrete subclasses (`ColonialHouse`, `ModernRanchHouse`).
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: An abstract class serves as a mandatory structural guideline; concrete subclasses turn that incomplete specification into fully functioning objects.

activities.content:
In enterprise application design, certain entities represent overarching domain concepts rather than tangible, standalone objects.

For example, in a banking platform:
- A `BankAccount` represents shared concepts (account number, balance, deposit logic).
- However, you never open a "generic bank account"; you always open a concrete `SavingsAccount` or `CheckingAccount`.

An abstract class models this domain foundation, serving as a template for specialized subclasses.

activities.title: Abstract Classes in Java: Definition, Mechanics, and Restrictions
Abstract Vehicle Blueprint with Shared State
activities.explanation: Vehicle provides common state (vin, fuelLevel) and concrete method refuel(). ElectricCar overrides the abstract drive() method to implement EV energy math.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: Attempting `new Vehicle(...)` fails at compile time because Vehicle is abstract.
`ElectricCar` extends `Vehicle` and invokes `super(vin, batteryKwh)` to initialize parent fields.
`ElectricCar` overrides `drive(...)`, satisfying the abstract method requirement.
Calling `myTesla.drive(100.0)` invokes child logic, while `myTesla.refuel(15.0)` invokes inherited concrete parent logic.

activities.title: Multilevel Abstract Class Hierarchy
activities.explanation: TwoDimensionalShape is also abstract, so it does not need to implement render(). Circle is the first concrete class, so it MUST implement render().

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `TwoDimensionalShape` extends `GraphicElement` and remains abstract, so it is not required to implement `render()`.
`Circle` is a concrete class; the compiler requires it to implement `render()`.
In `main`, upcasting to `GraphicElement` executes `Circle.render()` via dynamic dispatch.

questions.question: What occurs when the Java compiler encounters: `abstract class Base {} ... Base b = new Base();`?
options: It runs the default constructor and creates a Base instance
Compilation error: Base is abstract; cannot be instantiated
Runtime InstantiationException
A null reference is assigned to b
questions.explanation: The Java compiler strictly prevents direct instantiation of abstract classes, reporting 'Base is abstract; cannot be instantiated'.

questions.question: Can an abstract class declare a constructor in Java?
options: No, constructors cannot be written in abstract classes because they cannot be instantiated
Yes, abstract classes can have constructors called by subclass constructors via super()
Only if the constructor is marked abstract
Only private constructors are allowed
questions.explanation: Abstract classes have constructors to initialize their own fields when a subclass instance is created via `super()` constructor chaining.

questions.question: If class `Child` extends `abstract class Parent`, but does NOT implement all inherited abstract methods, what must `Child` do to compile?
options: Declare all unimplemented methods as private
Class Child must also be declared abstract
Provide dummy empty bodies automatically
Change the class name to start with 'Abstract'
questions.explanation: If a subclass does not implement all abstract methods from its superclass, it remains an incomplete blueprint and MUST be declared `abstract`.

questions.question: Which modifier combination is ILLEGAL for a class definition in Java?
options: public abstract class
abstract final class
abstract class
strictfp abstract class
questions.explanation: `final` means a class cannot be extended, while `abstract` demands that a class MUST be extended to be useful. They are direct logical opposites and forbidden together.

questions.question: Can an abstract class have instance variables (non-static fields)?
options: No, only constants (static final) are permitted
Yes, abstract classes can have full instance variables with any access modifier
Only primitive variables like int and double
Only protected variables
questions.explanation: Unlike interfaces (prior to Java default methods and static fields), abstract classes can declare instance state (`private`, `protected`, `public`) inherited by child objects.

questions.question: Can an abstract class contain static methods in Java?
options: No, abstract classes cannot contain static members
Yes, static methods can be defined and called directly using AbstractClass.staticMethod()
Only if the static method is also abstract
Only if invoked inside the subclass
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can declare static methods. They can be invoked directly on the class name without requiring any instance.

questions.question: What is the result of compiling: `abstract class A { abstract void f(); } class B extends A {}`?
options: Compilation successful; f() defaults to an empty body
Compilation error: B is not abstract and does not override abstract method f() in A
Runtime AbstractMethodError upon class loading
A warning is printed
questions.explanation: Class B is concrete but fails to provide an implementation for inherited abstract method `f()`, resulting in a compile-time error.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding reference variables of an abstract class type?
options: Abstract class reference variables cannot be declared
Abstract class reference variables can point to instances of any concrete subclass
They can only point to null
They can only call static methods
questions.explanation: An abstract class reference (e.g. `Vehicle v = new Car();`) can hold references to any concrete subclass instance, powering runtime polymorphism.

questions.question: Can an abstract method be declared `static`?
options: Yes, static abstract methods are supported since Java 8
No, static methods belong to the class and cannot be overridden; abstract requires overriding
Only in interface definitions
Only if the method has no parameters
questions.explanation: Static methods are bound at compile time and cannot be overridden dynamically. Therefore, `static abstract` is an illegal modifier combination.

questions.question: Can you declare a class abstract without writing any abstract methods inside it?
options: No, Java syntax requires at least one abstract method
Yes, it is completely valid and used to prevent direct instantiation of a base class
Only if the class extends another abstract class
Only if the class implements an interface
questions.explanation: A class can be declared `abstract` purely to prohibit direct instantiation, even if 100% of its methods are concrete.

interviewQA.question: Why can't an abstract class be instantiated if it has a constructor?
interviewQA.answer: An abstract class is conceptually incomplete. Even if it possesses a constructor to initialize its own instance fields, its abstract methods have no executable code. Allowing `new AbstractClass()` would risk callers invoking unimplemented methods, causing catastrophic crashes. The constructor exists solely to support `super()` calls during subclass instantiation.

interviewQA.question: Why is `final abstract class` a compilation error in Java?
interviewQA.answer: `final` specifies that a class cannot be extended by any other class. `abstract` specifies that the class is incomplete and must be extended by a subclass to be utilized. Because a class cannot be simultaneously un-extendable and require extension, the Java language specification explicitly forbids combining `final` and `abstract`.

interviewQA.question: How does Java handle constructor execution in an abstract class hierarchy?
interviewQA.answer: When a concrete subclass is instantiated with `new SubClass()`, the subclass constructor invokes `super(...)` either explicitly or implicitly. The JVM walks up the constructor chain to `java.lang.Object`, executes constructors downwards (Object -> AbstractClass -> SubClass), and fully initializes parent fields before executing the subclass constructor body.

interviewQA.question: Can a subclass of an abstract class also be declared abstract? When is this design used?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. An intermediate subclass can be declared abstract. It inherits the abstract methods of its parent and can choose to implement some, none, or introduce additional abstract methods. This is used in multilevel framework designs (e.g. `java.util.AbstractList` extends `java.util.AbstractCollection`) to progressively add partial implementation layers.

interviewQA.question: Can an abstract class implement an interface without implementing its methods?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. An abstract class that implements an interface is not required to implement the interface's abstract methods. It can pass that implementation responsibility down to its concrete subclasses.

interviewQA.question: Is it possible to declare an abstract class `private`?
interviewQA.answer: A top-level class cannot be declared `private` or `protected` in Java (only `public` or package-private). However, a nested (inner) class can be declared `private abstract`, accessible only within its enclosing outer class.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I know the exact syntax for declaring an abstract class using the abstract keyword.
I understand why direct instantiation `new MyAbstractClass()` causes a compiler error.
I know that abstract class reference variables can hold concrete child objects.
I understand why abstract classes can and do have constructors.
I know that concrete subclasses must implement all inherited abstract methods.
I understand why intermediate subclasses can remain abstract without implementing parent methods.
I know that `abstract final` is an illegal modifier combination.
I know that an abstract class can contain concrete methods, static methods, and fields.
I understand constructor execution order in abstract class hierarchies.
I can design a clean 2-tier or 3-tier abstract class inheritance tree.

practiceProblems.title: Abstract Employee Base with Pay Calculation
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Calculate employee pay using an abstract class:

1. Abstract Class Employee:
   - Field: protected String name
   - Constructor: Employee(String name)
   - Abstract Method: public abstract double calculatePay();

2. Subclasses extending Employee:
   - Class SalariedEmployee: constructor(name, monthlySalary), @Override calculatePay() returning monthlySalary
   - Class HourlyEmployee: constructor(name, hourlyRate, hoursWorked), @Override calculatePay() returning hourlyRate * hoursWorked

Test in Main:
Employee e1 = new SalariedEmployee("Alice", 4000.0);
Employee e2 = new HourlyEmployee("Bob", 25.0, 160.0);
Print '<name>: $' + e.calculatePay() for both employees.
hints: In Worker, add public abstract double calculateSalary();
In ContractWorker, calculateSalary returns basePay * hoursWorked;
practiceProblems.description: Define an abstract Employee base class where Salaried and Hourly employees compute their own pay.

practiceProblems.title: Abstract Bank Account with Transaction Audit
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a banking account system from scratch:

1. Abstract Class BankAccount:
   - Fields: protected String accountId, protected double balance
   - Constructor: BankAccount(String id, double balance)
   - Abstract Method: public abstract boolean withdraw(double amount);
   - Concrete Method: public void printBalance() printing '[<accountId>] Balance: $<formatted balance with 2 decimals>'

2. Class CheckingAccount (extends BankAccount):
   - Field: private double overdraftLimit
   - Constructor: CheckingAccount(id, balance, overdraft) calling super(id, balance)
   - Method: @Override public boolean withdraw(double amt): if amt <= balance + overdraftLimit, balance -= amt and return true; else return false

Test in Main:
CheckingAccount acc = new CheckingAccount("CHK-901", 100.0, 200.0);
acc.withdraw(150.0); acc.printBalance();.
hints: In CheckingAccount.withdraw, check if (balance + overdraftLimit >= amt).
Notice balance becomes -50.00 after withdrawing 200.0 from 150.0.
practiceProblems.description: Build an abstract BankAccount managing balance state and audited withdrawals from scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Database Connection Pooler
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a database connection manager from scratch:

1. Abstract Class DatabaseConnection:
   - Fields: protected String host, protected int port, protected String dbName
   - Constructor: DatabaseConnection(String host, int port, String db)
   - Abstract Method: public abstract String getJdbcUrl();
   - Concrete Method: public void connect() printing 'Connected to <getJdbcUrl()>'

2. Class PostgresConnection (extends DatabaseConnection):
   - Constructor: PostgresConnection(host, port, db) calling super(host, port, db)
   - Method: @Override public String getJdbcUrl() returning 'Postgres at jdbc:postgresql://' + host + ':' + port + '/' + dbName

Test in Main:
DatabaseConnection db = new PostgresConnection("localhost", 5432, "dev_db");
Call db.connect();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Connected to Postgres at jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/db
Executing Postgres query: SELECT * FROM metrics
hints: runReport is a concrete template method in DatabaseConnection that coordinates connect() and executeQuery(sql).
practiceProblems.description: Connect to Postgres and MySQL using a shared abstract DatabaseConnection parent from scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Illegal abstract final Combination
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Fix the compiler error: 'illegal combination of modifiers: abstract and final':

Bug: In EncryptionService, `abstract final String encrypt(String s)` combines contradictory keywords! `abstract` requires overriding, but `final` forbids overriding.

Your Task:
1. Remove `final` from the abstract method in EncryptionService.
2. Implement `@Override public String encrypt(String s)` in AesEncryptionService returning '[AES-256] ' + s.

Test in Main:
EncryptionService svc = new AesEncryptionService();
Print svc.encrypt("SECRET_DATA");.
hints: Remove final from final abstract class BaseCipher.
Change new BaseCipher(256) to new AesCipher(256).
practiceProblems.description: A method cannot be both abstract (must be overridden) and final (cannot be overridden). Fix the contradiction.

practiceProblems.title: GUI Button and Component Hierarchy
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a GUI component rendering hierarchy from scratch:

1. Abstract Class GuiComponent:
   - Field: protected String id
   - Constructor: GuiComponent(String id)
   - Abstract Method: public abstract void render();

2. Abstract Class AbstractButton (extends GuiComponent):
   - Field: protected String label
   - Constructor: AbstractButton(String id, String label) calling super(id)

3. Class PrimaryButton (extends AbstractButton):
   - Constructor: PrimaryButton(id, label) calling super(id, label)
   - Method: @Override public void render() printing '[PrimaryBtn ID: <id>] Rendering blue solid button: "<label>"'

Test in Main:
GuiComponent btn = new PrimaryButton("btn-login", "Login");
Call btn.render();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
[PrimaryBtn ID: btn-login] Rendering blue solid button: "Log In"
Button [Log In] clicked
hints: AbstractButton is an intermediate abstract class that extends UiComponent without implementing draw().
PrimaryButton is the concrete leaf class that implements draw().
practiceProblems.description: Render specialized primary and ghost buttons through an abstract GuiComponent parent from scratch.
